outputs.exact_statement: For every $q,R,J$ as above and every $\Delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ with the following property. Suppose that $\Lambda$ is a finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian [eq:hamiltonian] has a unique normalized ground vector $\Omega$, up to phase, with ground energy $E_0$, and satisfies $$H-E_0\mathop{\mathrm{id}}\ \ge\ \Delta\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{id}}-\lvert \Omega\rangle\langle \Omega\rvert\bigr).$$ Then for every $A\subseteq\Lambda$, $$\label{eq:area-law} S_\Omega(A)\le C\,|\partial_\Lambda A|.$$ The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.

The conclusion of Theorem 1 holds for every subset of a finite rectangular square lattice with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions and a unique ground state separated by a fixed global gap. For every domain covered by that theorem it also implies $$S_\Omega(A)\le4C|\partial_{\rm in}A|, \qquad S_\Omega(A)\le2C|Z_A|.$$

Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on finite-dimensional $D\otimes E$, and put $\delta=\tfrac12\lVert \rho-\sigma\rVert_1\le1$ and $d_D=\dim D$. Then $$\label{eq:conditional-continuity}
 |S(D|E)_\rho-S(D|E)_\sigma|
 \le2\delta\log d_D+(1+\delta)
                 h\left(\frac{\delta}{1+\delta}\right)
 \le C\sqrt\delta\log(e d_D).$$ The same estimates hold for $S(D)$ by making $E$ trivial. Summing the bounds for $S(D)$ and $S(D|E)$ therefore bounds the continuity cost for $I(D:E)$ in terms of $d_D$, independently of $\dim E$.
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, if $\partial_\Lambda A=\varnothing$, then $S_\Omega(A)=0$.

Let $\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{v\in V}\mathcal H_v$ be a finite tensor product of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Let $\mathsf H=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} h_i$, where $\mathcal I$ is finite, each $h_i$ is self-adjoint, $\lVert h_i\rVert\le c_0$ for a fixed $c_0\ge0$, and $h_i$ has a designated support $D_i\subseteq V$. Suppose that $\mathsf H$ has a one-dimensional ground space spanned by a normalized vector $\Psi$, ground energy $E_0$, and gap at least $g_0>0$. Fix a bipartition $B\sqcup B^c=V$. Let $\mathcal I_\times$ be the indices whose designated support meets both sides, and put $$\rho=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_{B^c}\lvert \Psi\rangle\langle \Psi\rvert,\qquad
 d_i=\prod_{v\in D_i}\dim\mathcal H_v,\qquad
 \mathcal B=1+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_\times}\log^2(\mathrm e d_i).$$ Let $p_j$ be the positive eigenvalues of $\rho$, let $K$ take the value $-\log p_j$ with probability $p_j$, and write $S=S(\rho)$ and $\vartheta=c_0/g_0$. Then $$\log\mathbb E\mathrm e^{uK}
 \le uS+512\mathrm e\,\vartheta\mathcal B u^2,
 \qquad
 |u|\le\frac{1}{32\sqrt{(1+\vartheta)\mathcal B}}.
 \label{eq:initial-tail-mgf}$$ Consequently, for every $w\ge0$, $$\Pr\{|K-S|>w\}
 \le \min\left\{1,\,
  2\mathrm e^{\mathrm e/2}
  \exp\left(-\frac{w}{32\sqrt{(1+\vartheta)\mathcal B}}\right)
              \right\}.
 \label{eq:initial-tail-probability}$$

There are integers $C_{\mathrm{pad}}\ge1$ and a constant $C_{\mathrm{buf}}$, depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta$, with the following property. Let $Q$ be safe, let $r\ge1$ be an integer, and let $Q_0$ be an integer rectangle of size at most $r$ such that $Q_0^{+C_{\mathrm{pad}}r}\subseteq Q$. Set $$X=A\cap Q_0,\qquad
 T=(A\cap Q_0^{+C_{\mathrm{pad}}r})\setminus X.$$ Then, in the original ground state $\Omega$, $$S(X\mid T)\le\frac12S(X)+C_{\mathrm{buf}}r.
 \label{eq:initial-buffer-discount}$$

There are constants $C<\infty$ and $e_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta$, such that $$F_{\mathrm{box}}(r)\le Cr^{1+e_0}\qquad(r\ge1).
 \label{eq:initial-box-bound}$$

Let $\tau_t(B)=e^{itH}Be^{-itH}$. There are positive constants $C,v,c$ such that, for every original support $X_i$, every operator $A$ supported in $X_i$, every site $y$, and every on-site operator $B_y$, $$\|[\tau_t(A),B_y]\|
 \le C\|A\|\|B_y\|e^{v|t|-c d_\Lambda(a_i,y)}.
 \label{eq:quasilocal-lr}$$ The commutator is zero when $d_\Lambda(a_i,y)=\infty$. Moreover, $$\|\tau_t(A)-E_{i,l}(\tau_t(A))\|
 \le \|A\|\min\{2,Ce^{v|t|-cl}\}.
 \label{eq:quasilocal-lr-ce}$$

Fix an integer $p\ge1$, put $\alpha=p/(p+1)$, and let $\delta>0$. Define the real even function $$\chi(\omega)=
 \begin{cases}
  e\exp[-(1-(\omega/\delta)^2)^{-p}],&|\omega|<\delta,\\
  0,&|\omega|\ge\delta.
 \end{cases}$$ Then $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$, $\chi(0)=1$, and the real even function $$f(t)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\chi(\omega)e^{-it\omega}\,d\omega$$ satisfies $$\chi(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(t)e^{it\omega}\,dt,
 \qquad |f(t)|\le Ce^{-c|t|^\alpha}.
 \label{eq:quasilocal-filter-decay}$$ Here $C,c>0$ depend only on $p,\delta$.

Suppose $H\Omega=E_0\Omega$, $\|\Omega\|=1$, and $$H-E_0I\ge\Delta(I-P_\Omega),\qquad
 P_\Omega=|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|.$$ For each integer $p\ge1$ and $\alpha=p/(p+1)$, there are operators $k_i$, indexed by the original supports and retaining their anchors, and a constant $c_*>0$ such that $$0\le k_i\le I,\qquad k_i\Omega=0,\qquad
 H_F:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}k_i
       \ge c_*^{-1}(H-E_0I)\ge g(I-P_\Omega),
 \qquad g:=\Delta/c_*.
 \label{eq:quasilocal-positive}$$ Thus $H_F$ has the unique ground vector $\Omega$, ground energy zero, and gap at least $g$. Furthermore, $$k_{i,l}:=E_{i,l}(k_i)\in[0,I],\qquad
 \|k_i-k_{i,l}\|\le Ce^{-cl^\alpha}
 \quad(l\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}).
 \label{eq:quasilocal-positive-tail}$$ Each $k_i$ is supported in the connected component containing $a_i$.

For the constraints of Proposition 10, define $$G_i=(I-k_i)^{1/2},\quad K_i=k_i^{1/2},\qquad G_{i,l}=(I-k_{i,l})^{1/2},\quad K_{i,l}=k_{i,l}^{1/2}.$$ These are positive contractions, $G_i\Omega=\Omega$, $K_i\Omega=0$, and $$\|G_i-G_{i,l}\|+\|K_i-K_{i,l}\|\le Ce^{-cl^\alpha}, \qquad G_{i,l}^2+K_{i,l}^2=I. \label{eq:quasilocal-root-tail}$$ Define maps on the full operator algebra by $$\mathcal E_i(B)=G_iBG_i+K_iBK_i,\qquad \mathcal E_{i,l}(B)=G_{i,l}BG_{i,l}+K_{i,l}BK_{i,l}.$$ Both maps are unital and completely positive, and are contractions in operator norm, also after tensoring with the identity map on any auxiliary matrix algebra. The completely bounded norm, denoted by $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$, is the supremum of the operator norms on all such auxiliary extensions. In this norm, $$\|\mathcal E_i-\mathcal E_{i,l}\|_{\mathrm{cb}} \le Ce^{-cl^\alpha}. \label{eq:quasilocal-channel-tail}$$ The map $\mathcal E_{i,l}$ fixes every operator commuting with the full algebra on $N_l(a_i)$, including operators supported outside that ball. All these conclusions allow arbitrary spectator auxiliary systems.

Use Proposition 10 with $p=1$, so $\alpha=1/2$. Fix $C_0>0$. There is a constant $C_1$, depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta,C_0$, with the following property for every real $n\ge2$ and every nonempty $S_0\subseteq\Lambda$ with $|S_0|\le C_0n^2$. Put $r_0=\lceil C_1(\log n)^2\rceil$. If $d_i^0:=d_\Lambda(a_i,S_0)<\infty$, define $$r_i=\max\{r_0,\lfloor d_i^0/2\rfloor\},\qquad \widetilde h_i=k_{i,r_i},\qquad \widetilde X_i=N_{r_i}(a_i). \label{eq:quasilocal-variable-radius}$$ If $d_i^0=\infty$, set $\widetilde h_i=k_i$ and designate its anchor’s entire component as $\widetilde X_i$. Then $\widetilde H=\sum_i\widetilde h_i$ is a sum of positive contractions and $$\|\widetilde H-H_F\|\le\epsilon_n, \qquad \epsilon_n:=\min\{n^{-1000},g/4\}. \label{eq:quasilocal-truncation-error}$$ Its ground energy $\widetilde E_0$ lies in $[0,\epsilon_n]$, its ground vector $\widetilde\Omega$ is unique, and its gap is at least $g/2$. After a choice of phase, $$\|\widetilde\Omega-\Omega\|\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n/g},\qquad \frac12\big\||\widetilde\Omega\rangle\langle\widetilde\Omega| -P_\Omega\big\|_1\le\sqrt{2\epsilon_n/g}. \label{eq:quasilocal-ground-distance}$$* *For a set $X\subseteq S_0$, let $b_X=|\partial_\Lambda X|$ and let $\mathcal C_X$ be the labels whose designated supports $\widetilde X_i$ meet both $X$ and $\Lambda\setminus X$. Every such support has radius exactly $r_0$, and $$|\mathcal C_X|\le Cb_X(r_0+1)^2,\qquad \log d_i\le C(r_0+1)^2\quad(i\in\mathcal C_X),\qquad d_i:=q^{|\widetilde X_i|}. \label{eq:quasilocal-crossing-count}$$ Consequently the cut parameter $$\mathcal B_X:=1+\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_X}\log^2(e d_i) \le C(1+b_X)(r_0+1)^6. \label{eq:quasilocal-cut-budget}$$ In particular, $b_X\le C_2nD$ and $D\ge1$ imply $\mathcal B_X\le CnD(\log n)^{12}$, with the constant also depending on $C_2$.

Let $\theta$ be a unit pure vector on $P,x,U,F$, put $Y=xU$, and write $\rho_D$ for its marginals. Suppose $P=P_0P_1$ and that $0\le h\le I$ is supported on $P_0x$. Set $$d_h=(\dim P_0)(\dim x),\qquad \ell_h=\log(ed_h),\qquad
 \eta=I(x:F|U)_\theta=I(x:F|P)_\theta.$$ Define the entire scalar function $$f(z)=\langle\theta,
       \rho_P^{[z]}\rho_Y^{[-z]}h
       \rho_P^{[-z]}\rho_Y^{[z]}\theta\rangle.$$ There are universal constants $c,C>0$ such that for $0<a\ell_h\le c$ and $t=a/2$, $$\label{eq:conditional-skew}
 |f(t)|-\Re f(t)\le C a^2\ell_h^4\eta^{1/8}.$$ In particular the left side is zero if $\eta=0$.

Fix a partition $P,Y,F$ of $\mathcal V$, $0[replicas:leaf-metric], and define on $\mathcal S_k$ $$O_k=A_k^{-1/2}\bar h A_k^{1/2},\qquad f_\theta=\langle\theta, \rho_P^t\rho_Y^{-t}h\rho_P^{-t}\rho_Y^t\theta\rangle,$$ where $\rho_Q$ is the $Q$ marginal of $\theta$. All powers in $f_\theta$ are zero on kernels. Then $\sup_k\lVert O_k\rVert<\infty$, with a bound allowed to depend on the fixed entire system and $h$. For every fixed noncommutative polynomial $q$ in two variables, $$\label{replicas:polynomial-symbol} \sup_{\sigma} \left|\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\sigma q(O_k,O_k^\dagger) -\int q(f_\theta,\overline{f_\theta})\,d\mu_\sigma(\theta) \right|\longrightarrow0,$$ where the supremum is over all density matrices on $\mathcal S_k$. Moreover, for $\mathcal D_k=|O_k|+|O_k^\dagger|-O_k-O_k^\dagger$, $$\label{replicas:skew-symbol} \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\sigma\mathcal D_k =2\int\bigl(|f_\theta|-\operatorname{Re}f_\theta\bigr) \,d\mu_\sigma(\theta)+o_k(1),$$ uniformly in $\sigma$.* *If $0\le h\le I$ has a designated supporting subsystem of dimension $d_h$, put $x=Y\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}h$, $Y_0=Y\setminus x$, and $$\eta_\theta=S_\theta(x|P)+S_\theta(x|Y_0) =I_\theta(x:F|P)=I_\theta(x:F|Y_0).$$ Here the designated support may replace the minimal support in the definition of $x$. If $a\log(e d_h)\le c$, then $$\label{replicas:skew-bound} \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\sigma\mathcal D_k \le C a^2\log^C(e d_h) \int\eta_\theta^{1/8}\,d\mu_\sigma(\theta) +o_k(1).$$ The assertion also holds with the two outer parts exchanged.

Under [scanner:scales]–[scanner:test-geometry], the preceding construction has the following properties for all sufficiently large $n$.* 1. *Every splitting designated support is a graph $r_0$-ball wholly inside $A$. It splits at most one band, and there it meets $Y$ and exactly one of the two sides. The metric algebras generated by all statuses of distinct bands commute on the symmetric replica space.* 2. *Every assigned site of $A$ has oriented depth at most $j+D+r_0$ on its side. Each actual set $U$ or $UY$ is comparable by inclusion with a deterministic positive-depth prefix, and differs from that prefix by at most $CnD$ sites. The cuts of $U,UY,Y,P_0,V$ have at most $CnD$ edges. At most $CKnD$ terms split in any joint status.* 3. *For every labelled term $i$, every round, and every common $p$, the sum of the full terminal-leaf probabilities on which it splits is at most $CD/m$.* 4. *An old history is called good if no side has an assigned site of $A$ of oriented depth greater than $j+D/2$. For every fixed $M>0$, the probability of a history failing this condition at any time is at most $n^{-M}$, for sufficiently large $n$. At a charge round on a good old history, each split term is sampled on its splitting side with probability at least $c/(nD)$.* *All probabilities here are the classical path probabilities of the history tree, before the transport of replica states.

Assume [scanner:scales] and [scanner:test-geometry], and let $00$ is fixed, and suppose $a r_0^2$ is sufficiently small. Construct the auxiliary systems, the fixed label sector, and the unnormalized vector $\mathrm{pre}$ as in Proposition 24, using typical width $w=n^{3/5}$. For each sufficiently large replica count $k$, there are a charge round and a common parameter $p_k\in[\epsilon/2,\epsilon]$ at which the normalized vector $v_k=\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}/N$, $s=1/4$, has defect energy $$E_{{\rm def},k} =\frac{\langle v_k,\overline{\widetilde H}v_k\rangle -\widetilde E_0}{\widetilde g}$$ bounded by $$E_{{\rm def},k} \le Cn^\ell D^2W^2(\log n)^C \bigl(\delta_n^{1/8}+\epsilon+n^{-100}\bigr) +Cn^{-1000}+o_k(1), \label{scanner:energy-output}$$ where $$\delta_n=C_e\epsilon^{-1} \bigl(n^{e-\mu}+a^{1/4}(\log n)^C\bigr). \label{scanner:density-output}$$ Here $\overline{\widetilde H}$ is the mean of the physical Hamiltonian over the copies. All norm comparisons of Proposition 24 apply at the selected points, with shell entropy bound $B_{\rm sh}\le C_e(nL^e+n)$, mismatch $B_{\rm exc}\le CnD$, and marginal parameter $\mathcal B\le CnD(\log n)^C$. The sharp comparisons additionally require their stated condition on $a\sqrt{\mathcal B}$.* *The entire finite physical system, $n$, the scan, and all auxiliary dimensions are fixed before $k\to\infty$. The remainder is uniform over the selected round and parameter, although these may depend on $k$. Constants may depend on the fixed exponents and the input constant $C_e$.

For $C_{\rm tpl}$ sufficiently large, a template satisfies $$|T|\le Cns_0,\qquad
 |T_j\setminus T_{j-1}|\le n\quad(1\le j\le s_0),
 \qquad |\partial_{\mathbb Z^2}T_j|\le Cn\quad(0\le j\le s_0).
 \label{scanner:template-geometry}$$ Suppose it is separated from the cut and, for some $0<e<1$, $F_{\rm box}(r)\le C_e r^{1+e}$ for every integer $r\ge1$. Then, for every integer $1\le L\le s_0$, $$S_\Omega(X)\le C'_e ns_0^e,\qquad
 S_\Omega(Q_j)\le C'_e nL^e\quad(0\le j\le L).
 \label{scanner:template-entropy}$$ The same shell bound, with an additional $Cn$, holds for any prefix obtained by including all depth rows before one row and an arbitrary subset of that last row. All physical cuts of $X,Q_j$, and $A\cap T_j$ have $O(n)$ edges.

There is a constant $C$, depending only on the Hamiltonian parameters, such that $$F_{\rm box}(r)\le Cr^{1+e_*}\quad(r\ge1),
 \qquad e_*=2\cdot10^{-6}.$$

Let $T$ be a template separated from the cut, with parameters $(n,s_0)$ as in Definition 27. Set $$L=\lfloor n^{1-10^{-5}}\rfloor, \qquad X=A\cap T, \qquad S_0=A\cap T_L,$$ and suppose $L\le s_0$. For all sufficiently large $n$, $$I_\Omega(X:\Lambda\setminus S_0) \le C n^{1-\varepsilon},\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-5}. \label{scanner:collar-output}$$ The constant and threshold are independent of $T,s_0,n,\Lambda$, and $A$. The cuts of $X,S_0$, and $S_0\setminus X$ have $O(n)$ edges, and $|S_0|=O(n^2)$.

Let $\psi$ be a pure state on a finite tensor product with site set $\Lambda$. Suppose that $$A=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal I_0}X_i
       \mathbin{\dot\cup}\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal I_1}X_i
 \subseteq\Lambda$$ is a partition into disjoint sets, and fix an order on each finite index set $\mathcal I_f$, $f\in\{0,1\}$. Write $B=\Lambda\setminus A$. If $$I_\psi\left(X_i:B\cup
       \bigcup_{\substack{j\in\mathcal I_f\\j<i}}X_j\right)
 \le \varepsilon_i
 \qquad(i\in\mathcal I_f),$$ then $$S_\psi(A)\le S_\psi(D)+\frac12\sum_i\varepsilon_i.$$

Fix the constants $D_0$ and $C_{\mathrm{tpl}}$ in Definition 27, and a lower scale threshold $n_*\ge1$. There is a constant $C$ with the following property. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite induced subgraph of the square lattice, let $A\subseteq\Lambda$, and suppose that $b=|\partial_\Lambda A|>0$. Let $Z$ be the set of endpoints of those cut edges.* *There are a set $D\subseteq A$, a finite ordered collection of disjoint nonempty sets $X_i\subseteq A$, labels $f_i\in\{0,1\}$, ambient templates $T_i\subset\mathbb Z^2$, and integers $n_i\ge n_*$ such that:* 1. *$A=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bigcup_iX_i$ and $|D|\le Cb$.* 2. *$X_i\subseteq A\cap T_i$. Each $T_i$ is a template of Definition 27: it is a union of $N_i$ lattice samples of closed convex rectangles or triangles with side slopes $0,\infty,1,-1$, each of sup-norm diameter at most $s_i$, where $$\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_\infty T_i\le n_i,\qquad n_i\ge C_{\mathrm{tpl}}N_i(s_i+1),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(T_i,Z)>4D_0s_i.$$ Moreover $L_i=\lfloor n_i^{1-\ell}\rfloor\le s_i$.* 3. *The templates satisfy $$\begin{aligned} \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(T_i,Z)&>2n_i^\beta,\label{geometry:cut-clearance}\\ \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty\left(T_i, \bigcup_{\substack{j2n_i^\beta.\label{geometry:ordered-clearance} \end{aligned}$$ As usual, the distance to the empty set is infinite.* 4. *The scale losses are summable: $$\sum_i n_i^{-100}\le Cb.$$* *The constant $C$ may depend on the fixed template constants and on $n_*$, but not on the domain or cut.

There is an absolute constant $a_0>0$, independent of the layer and the chosen shifts, such that, on taking $k_0$ sufficiently large:*

1.  *Distinct marks $v,w$ satisfy $\lVert v-w\rVert_\infty\ge a_0\max(S_v,S_w)$.*

2.  *In the square $v+[-a_0S_v,a_0S_v]^2$, all active boundaries are straight rays from $v$ in the eight axis and diagonal directions. Each sector between consecutive active rays has one tile identifier, and consecutive sectors have opposite labels. If there is no active ray, the square is in one tile.*

*An active boundary here means an interface of distinct identifiers; seams removed by a merge are not boundaries.

For a sufficiently small fixed choice of $a_0$ and the corresponding threshold $S_*$, every active mark $(v,S)$ at every generation has a terminal-square-free isolated star $v+[-a_0S,a_0S]^2$ with the properties of Lemma 35. Distinct active marks satisfy the same separation inequality. The simultaneous removal squares are disjoint. Each replacement has opposite labels across every positive-length interface of distinct identifiers, and its same-label contacts with old remnants or peer replacements occur only at marks of the next generation. Every descendant mark and every descendant birth region of a mark $(v,S)$ lies within sup distance $2d(S)$ of $v$. Each branch terminates after finitely many generations.

There is a fixed $c_1>0$ such that the following holds. Let $\mathcal B$ be the closed birth region of an initial belt tile of side scale $u=t_k$, or of a replacement tile whose removal square has halfside $u$. Then its distance from the final actual region of every earlier or peer identifier of the same label is at least $c_1u^{\rho_0}$. A peer means another initial belt tile, or another replacement born at the same generation, respectively.
